findings.summary: Staged per-chunk ISR evidence has no stable bounded commit rule.

Handle uncertain replies and takeover without reopening a prepared root. Alternatively specify a real freeze/invalidation generation observed by every membership writer. Add checks and caught mutants for join without roots, late writes, stale proof/epoch and commit/promotion races; never pretend staged reads are an atomic ISR vector.

findings.summary: Pair revocation has no bounded linearization predicate that every receiver admission/publication must compare.
findings.evidence: design.md:38–41 promises pair revocation by relationship-generation and destination-epoch changes, but a pair may own many relationships; contracts.md:29–33 and design.md:68–73 make CommitShip compare only relationship/ship/incarnation/epoch/ISR evidence, not the pair record/config generation. No atomic fanout or bounded revocation barrier is specified. A commit racing or preceding its relationship fanout can still publish for a revoked pair. ConfigureDrPair also changes the generation to which live sessions are pinned.
findings.fix: Make one pair-record CAS (generation+1/revoked) the O(1) revocation/configuration linearization point. Bind pair UUID and admitted config generation into every ship/receiver grant; compare that exact unrevoked pair revision in AttachStandby and every CommitShip/prepare-publication decision. Define bounded linearizable per-request/batch admission and connection invalidation; already admitted writes may finish only in isolated roots and can never publish after the pair CAS. Epoch cleanup across relationships is resumable fallout, not the authority barrier. Specify TLS1.3 fresh peer verification/no resumptions or generation-isolated session caches. Add CAS races for multiple relationships, stale sessions/queued frames, lost revocation response and metadata outage; catch a mutation omitting the pair compare.

findings.summary: A generic local target capability and a metadata-only ordinary Attach refusal do not isolate the specialized standby writer from ordinary device/maintenance paths.
findings.evidence: design.md:31–36 and contracts.md:26–28 return a local target token from AttachStandby, with no purpose claim or distinct ticket. Only ordinary metadata Attach is named as refused. Baseline Engine::start_target accepts a matching volume/node/epoch token (engine.rs:1595–1622); replica session accept binds those same claims (session.rs:135–156). Current #17 AttachMaintenance/StartMaintenance independently issue the ordinary capability, and #15/CSI/control shortcuts may reuse an existing attachment. #54 contracts explicitly needed a distinct FLRT and typed restore attachment to prevent the analogous bypass.
findings.fix: Define a purpose-bound standby receiver ticket (or an equivalently complete capability/mode contract) binding destination first epoch, relationship/generation, ship, pair generation, receiver node and writer epoch. Ordinary engine/control/ublk/agent/CSI and maintenance paths reject it and refuse Standby/Promoting independently; only typed receiver input admits inactive-root operations. Specify its exact token/mode handoff, slot accounting, status/device-info/detach answers and restart behavior using current #15/#17/#48/#54 seams, with whoever-lands-second integration. Add ordinary attach/token reuse, maintenance takeover, existing-device CSI shortcut and stale writer tests plus a caught ordinary-exposure mutation.

findings.summary: Local DR RPC authority and standby creation bypass the current tenancy role/owner contract as written.
findings.evidence: design.md:31–36 and contracts.md:19–39 say local administrator/read role only without #73 before/after activation rows or insecure refusal. CreateStandby has no owner semantics, although #73 requires system-provisioner and a system owner for ownerless creation, forbids tenant-form system names, and conditionally compares authorization/owner allocation state. Choose concrete existing roles, keeping security/deletion/audit-only identities from unintended DR mutation. Define this increment as system-owned standby creation through #76 with #73 system-provisioner, system owner and tenant-name refusal (or specify a complete tenant creation path). Define exhaustion/disconnect behavior preserving the last point and source pins. Add stalled TLS/Hello/truncated-body/flood/large-manifest and reservation-exhaustion fixtures showing bounded memory/work and continuing local application/heartbeat progress. findings.summary: The source worker has no operation that binds its newly constructed manifest into Outgoing before completion verification.
findings.evidence: contracts.md:66-69,83-88; lifecycle.md:54-57,72-73,182-188; wire-contracts.md:268-271. StartShip accepts a target snapshot and optional prior base hash, not the target manifest. The worker constructs that manifest later. ReportDrProgress accepts only bytes/error, and no other source RPC writes the manifest or enters Sending. RecordDrCompletion nevertheless must compare the receipt manifest against the outgoing tuple.
findings.fix: Add an exact worker-owned idempotent manifest-binding RPC (or extend ReportDrProgress explicitly) before foreign Begin. Validate canonical ManifestRootV1 against the authorized target/base refs and outgoing immutable destination, CAS the current noncancelled outgoing to a manifest-bound Sending state, persist the root/hash, and define identical/conflicting retry behavior. Specify how close barriers advance the outgoing to Closed. Add construct/bind/send/restart/lost-reply/conflicting-manifest/completion fixtures.

findings.summary: The replica ABI cannot install and later recover the manifest commitment needed to authenticate pages and receipts.
findings.evidence: wire-contracts.md:145-164,172-181; root-format.md:80,103-107,118-124,131-138,154-155; contracts.md:73,91-93. CreateRoot carries no ManifestRootV1; PutRootManifestPage carries only a page and sibling path. ManifestRootV1 first arrives at PrepareRoot, after pages/ranges must already have verified proofs and durable receipts. RootDescriptor/RootSeal retain only manifest_id, RootBlob retains pages/proofs, and metadata Admit retains only refs/hash/page count. No local read operation returns the full manifest root or persisted manifest pages/proofs for takeover/catch-up, despite the required complete copy/reconciliation. A SHA256 manifest_id cannot recover its Merkle root/preimage.
findings.fix: Define an immutable manifest-init/bind operation before any page/range ACK, its exact durable root/blob/journal representation (including the complete bounded ManifestRootV1), and replay/order/idempotency rules. Add bounded local get-manifest-root/page-proof operations for takeover and base-first catch-up, with typed session/root correlation and proof validation before receipt admission. Cover empty incremental manifests, crash before seal, restart on another node and joining-member transfer without contacting the foreign sender in vectors/crash/model fixtures.

findings.summary: Grant creation is not serialized with source cancellation, allowing a cancelled ship to acquire a new reader grant.
findings.evidence: lifecycle.md:167-171,199-205,332-335; #52 contracts.md Reader grant/RPC/lifecycle and Transactions: AuthorizeSnapshotRead compares header/catalog/reader, with no DR outgoing predicate. StartShip queues the outgoing and then creates target/base grants one at a time before recording their references. CancelShip can mark it Cancelled and close the grants currently present while an earlier handler subsequently creates another deterministic grant or has not yet published its reference. The defined #52 close barrier cannot prevent creation of a different/absent grant.
findings.fix: Extend the internal DR grant-claim transaction to compare the exact current noncancelled outgoing and source guard, and atomically publish its GrantRef or a durable per-kind claim. Cancellation must block further claims first and discover/close both deterministic grant identities even across a crash before reference publication; Closed/EndDrSource must require this phase complete. State transaction counts and test cancel before/between/after each target/base grant claim and reference update, including restart and lost response; add a caught late-grant-after-cancel mutation.

findings.summary: Deletion assigns relationship states that its enum does not define.
findings.evidence: lifecycle.md:82 says deletion marks the relationship Closed/Cancelled; contracts.md:38-40 defines only STANDBY, PROMOTING, PROMOTED, REVOKED (SOURCE_PAIRED is explicitly not a relationship state). CANCELLED exists only on Incoming and Outgoing.
findings.fix: Specify deletion as a concrete existing relationship state (for example REVOKED with generation/fence change), or allocate a terminal relationship state and define its RPC/status/retry behavior. Keep incoming/outgoing cancellation separate and add the terminal enum to deletion/recreation fixtures.

findings.summary: Closure retries do not define the already-CLOSED path after eligible grant collection.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/58/contracts.md:179-180 requires every CancelShip retry to invoke the reconciler for either terminal outcome; :188-194 defines that reconciler only for Committed/Cancelled/Closing, says lost replies repeat its read-back, and treats a missing COMPLETED grant as Internal. Yet :199-203 explicitly permits collecting grants once outgoing is CLOSED and only names EndDrSource as accepting that absence. A lost final closure reply followed by retry can therefore encounter CLOSED with collected grants and has no successful idempotent transition under these predicates.
findings.fix: Define an already-CLOSED fast path for ReportDrProgress(check_closure=true) and the reconciler used by CancelShip: return the unchanged durable outcome/all-closed mask without re-closing collected grants. Restrict missing-completed-grant=Internal to operations that have not durably established closure. Add lost final closure reply -> collection -> progress/cancel retry fixtures for both terminal outcomes.

findings.summary: The identical bind retry condition ambiguously requires COMPLETED on SENDING.

findings.summary: Socket-readiness exclusion can suppress genuine stalls forever; shaper waiting can also trigger false connection/header timeouts.
findings.evidence: #59 design.md:80–85 advances upload idle elapsed only when 'window/budget/socket readiness permit sending'. A peer that stops reading makes the socket nonwritable, so remote-progress idle never reaches120s. Conversely, cap min1byte/sec (line40) can delay even a TCP SYN beyond connect30s, independently of the userspace payload limiter. No concrete way to distinguish qdisc wait, TCP progress and server response progress is specified.
findings.fix: Define phase-specific eligible elapsed and observable progress events. Exclude only explicit local pacing/gate suspension, count remote-caused backpressure as stall time, and account for shaper delay in connect/header/response timing. Identify the actual connector/transport signals used. Add tests for a peer that accepts but never reads, a full send buffer, a server that consumes but never responds, and a1byte/sec handshake/response with qualified local shaping.

findings.summary: SDK admission/progress/cancellation remains an unspecified implementation gate.
findings.evidence: #59 design.md:49–54,80–87,171–178 and decisions.md's historical SDK gate still ask whether the chosen SDK exposes needed controls. findings.summary: The 'pacing only delays work' integration does not preserve #53's deadline and automatic-completion behavior.
findings.evidence: #59 design.md:97–109 only says to check retention and use #52's original commit protocol. Current #53 design.md:80–107 and contracts.md 'One root per operation' require store-time D/E, at most one re-cover, a pre-PUT allowance, and permanent incomplete status for a root accepted late, requiring an administrator's abort and a new operation. A gate may defer the root PUT over a closed window after its deadline check; a tiny cap can make root transmission itself exceed D. These are realistic configured cases where this living run cannot finish automatically even after the link returns.
findings.fix: Specify the exact #53-aware admission sequence after every limiter/window wait: refresh qualified store time, revalidate/renew exact-version retention, budget cover/root transfer under the policy, and never dispatch a known-stale root. Preserve #53's one-root/late-root semantics; explicitly diagnose incompatible budget/policy or the unavoidable late-root terminal outcome instead of promising unconditional eventual completion. Add close-during-cover, close-before-root, low-rate large-root, lost-root-ACK and late-root tests.

findings.summary: A sender's shaper does not prove the same arbitrary-interval envelope at the remote arrival point.
findings.evidence: #59 spec.md:35–38 requires bytes<=R*dt+B at the remote observation point; design.md:58–65 shapes the local namespace and captures remotely. A downstream queue can accumulate shaped traffic and release it in a burst larger than B, even when local departures satisfy the envelope. No path delay/buffering assumption or enlarged remote B is defined.
findings.fix: Choose an exact authoritative enforcement/observation boundary. Either guarantee the envelope at the owned local egress and treat remote arrival captures as diagnostics, marking the spec adjustment unapproved, or define and qualify downstream buffering/jitter bounds and include them in the remote envelope. Add a delayed/batched-path counterexample to the qualification tests.

findings.summary: S6's bounded resume/control traffic has no concrete accounting bound or resume protocol.
findings.evidence: #59 spec.md:57–61 requires separately bounded control/manifest traffic; design.md:97–101 gives only K and 'small bounded protocol overhead', and115–116 provides a counter. Current #52 contracts.md:383–399 permits encoded blocks up to4194384 bytes and pages/roots up to1048656 bytes;429–433 requires revalidating previously referenced versions, while a lost PUT can require a full exact-version GET. findings.fix: State the exact encoded in-flight payload bound K*(4194304+80), separately define page/root/control and verification-GET budgets/counts as functions of the bounded archive graph, and define what the 'resume episode' ends at. Count both directions and requests before the first new upload, distinguish retransmitted PUT payload from required GET readback, and add large-manifest/receipt-revalidation/lost-ACK fixtures. Keep the outbound cap boundary explicit.

findings.summary: The TCP-only gate black-holes PMTU feedback on ordinary lower-MTU WAN paths.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/59/transport-profile.md:38-46 fixes namespace/veth MTU1500 and only endpoint /32 routes; :131-140 permits only reverse TCP input, dropping ICMP including fragmentation-needed. A host/tunnel/downstream path with MTU below1500 can pass SYN and small records but drop full-sized DF TCP segments; no per-endpoint route MTU/MSS clamp, PMTU ICMP exception or PLPMTUD profile is specified. The 8334 co-located lab endpoint does not exercise this. Linux6.6 TCP explicitly handles ICMP_FRAG_NEEDED to update PMTU/MSS and retransmit: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.6/net/ipv4/tcp_ipv4.c (tcp_v4_mtu_reduced/tcp_v4_err); https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v6.6/networking/ip-sysctl.html documents PMTU/PLPMTUD controls.
findings.fix: Specify a narrow, lease/window-bound ICMP fragmentation-needed input rule validated against the owned TCP tuples/quoted packet, or a concrete conservative route-MTU/MSS/PLPMTUD scheme with qualification/refusal rules. Preserve object-only isolation and outbound accounting. Add a separate routed endpoint behind a smaller-MTU hop and assert large TLS/object traffic progresses; include forged ICMP and gate-closed counterexamples.

findings.summary: Supported payload-v1 modes have no defined phase-clock or #53 publication-cost calculation.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/59/design.md:45-48 permits payload-v1 at1B/s and without any rate for window-only admission. transport-profile.md:95 defines r=floor(99*R/100) only for wire-v1; :267-284 uses division by r for all phase allowances, and :304-310 defines the only local_cost via r/Q/wire_budget. policy-contracts.md:59-74 applies its emission-cost/window reservation and root_local_emit_seconds=ceil(local_cost(...)/1e9) without a profile branch to immutable repositories. At payload rate1 the borrowed wire r is zero; with no cap it is undefined. These valid configurations cannot follow the stated admission contract, and the wire-only queue/qualification failure rules do not specify a payload alternative.
findings.fix: Define profile-specific transport/phase clocks and local emission estimates: payload-v1 should use its actual optional payload rate/body budget and no kernel-shaper allowance, while window-only mode must explicitly define the zero known pacing cost plus bounded dispatch/window checks without asserting a minimum network throughput. Bind #53 finishing reservations to that profile-specific function. Add payload1B/s and payload-window-only immutable-root admission fixtures, including low-rate incompatibility, window closure, remote backpressure and no division by absent/zero rate.

rounds.resolution: Both findings addressed: narrowly leased owned-flow PMTU feedback plus routed/forged/closed-gate fixtures; profile-specific payload phase/cost/reserved-credit/no-rate branches preserving53 admission. Revisions unapproved; fresh combined R3 required.

findings.summary: Retry behavior and the subordinate-error wire extension do not match the current shared contract.
findings.evidence: #60 design.md:10-11,56-62,76-81,105-111 requires structured details to stop cycling, adds an ambiguously named reason and mentions bounded RetryAfter without a type, unit, numeric bound or wire field. #50 contracts.md:44-57 fixes INSTANCE_UNAVAILABLE=Unavailable, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE=ResourceExhausted, DENIED=PermissionDenied and INVALID_ENVELOPE=FailedPrecondition; ErrorInfo.reason is Kind, and retry is decided by gRPC code alone. findings.summary: The registry coverage check is not connected to the production configuration path it must cover.
findings.evidence: #60 S1 and intent outcome 2 require every configurable source to appear in conformance coverage. design.md:17-21,42-45 compares RegisteredKinds() to a FixtureFactory map but defines neither the production registry nor how startup construction is constrained by it. No RegisteredKinds/KeySource registry exists in the current source; meta/cmd/flaminio-meta/main.go:84-151 constructs options directly. #50 design.md:193-204 proposes the --kek-file construction path, while #57 design.md:27-32 adds a material-loader mode that still constructs cryptographic kind static. State how file-static and tpm-sealed-static loaders both resolve static, and add startup/configuration tests rejecting unregistered/fault kinds. findings.summary: Unpublished creation tests require a stable DEK that #50 and #76 deliberately do not persist.
findings.evidence: #60 design.md:92-94 requires the hidden create to retain its original operation/key identity and says retry cannot generate a different published key. Current #50 design.md:81-87,99-111 generates a DEK immediately before publication; with #76 a failed wrap leaves the operation and a helper wraps its own key at conditional finalization. #76 spec.md:43-57/design.md Conditional helpers retain the operation, admitted plan and claim revision, not an unpublished DEK. There is no prior durable key/envelope for a retry after failed initial Wrap to reuse.
findings.fix: Distinguish durable create identity from DEK identity. Before successful finalization, retries/helpers may generate independent candidate DEKs and must clear losers; only one atomic finalization may publish its bound envelope. After publication, recovery/retry must retain that exact winning envelope/key. Test failed wrap, competing helpers and lost publication reply with these assertions, without adding durable plaintext or another key-staging protocol.

findings.summary: The no-key-call I/O proof lacks a concrete route between the Go fault source and the Rust memory-node harness.
findings.evidence: #60 design.md:95-97,101-108,118-127 promises zero provider calls while memory-node read/write/resync/ISR executes, but names no Rust engine test file or bridge to its Go conformance/fault_source.go counters. Existing flaminio-node/tests/engine.rs:34-50,196-235 uses its own Rust FakeMeta through MetaPort, not a Go metadata service; its TLS network connects replicas. Existing Rust/Go tests are separate: flaminio-metaclient/tests/interop.rs:22-25 is ignored by ordinary cargo test and scripts/dev/meta-interop.sh:24-40 starts an ordinary production server without a test fault source. Thus the current fixture descriptions do not explain how the claimed counters observe the I/O path.
findings.fix: Name a runnable layered proof: ordinary Rust engine tests extend FakeMeta to count/script ReleaseVolumeKey and assert no further release during verified I/O/resync/ISR, while Go backend/mTLS tests prove a release invokes the counted source only as specified. Alternatively define an isolated test-binary server exposing the Go fixture to the Rust client/engine. Specify file/target wiring and keep test fault configuration out of shipping binaries; do not claim an unconnected Go counter proves Rust behavior.

findings.summary: The design presents an invented 1024-byte envelope ceiling as #50's exact bound.
findings.evidence: #60 design.md:23-26 says to consume #50's exact limits and then specifies envelope<=1024 bytes. #50 contracts.md:8-14,29-36 defines 1..64 ASCII identifier bytes per source component, profile 1..32 ASCII bytes and exactly 92 Sealed bytes for static. Its protobuf Size section bounds KeyEnvelope at 328 bytes with maximal fields; it defines no generic 1024-byte envelope representation. Tests based only on the stated 1024 ceiling would miss a static 93-byte sealed body or invalid identity bounds.
findings.fix: Use the shared field/encoding bounds directly: fixed/derived static identity, 64-byte DEK, 32-byte KEK, 92-byte Sealed and the shared protobuf size fixtures. Remove the unexplained generic 1024 limit, or explicitly propose and measure a separately versioned shared limit for future providers instead of attributing it to #50.

findings.summary: The required no-network claim contradicts the specified local integration fixtures.
findings.evidence: #60 intent outcome 5 and spec.md:62-64 say required tests run without network, while design.md:85 requires real loopback mTLS and :127 allows only that network exception. Actual backend helper meta/service/service_test.go:46-53 starts embedded etcd whose client and peer URLs are loopback HTTP (meta/kv/kvtest/kvtest.go:24-43); Rust memory-node tests also bind replica TCP/TLS listeners (flaminio-node/tests/engine.rs:196-209). These tests are feasible locally but not under the literal stated network restriction.
findings.fix: Say without external network, cloud/emulator services or credentials; explicitly permit owned loopback metadata mTLS, embedded-etcd client/peer traffic and replica TLS fixtures. Align intent, S9 and the design exception without weakening the prohibition on default cloud actions.

findings.summary: Conformance failure paths do not require unconditional cleanup of returned secret buffers.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/60/design.md:31-35 clears only successfully returned buffers after assertion. A broken source being tested can return a non-nil plaintext buffer together with an error, and an assertion can terminate the subtest before a subsequent clear. Neither case is named by the output-ownership tests, despite docs/issues/50/contracts.md:21-24 requiring caller-owned plaintext to be cleared on every exit and #60 S2 inheriting that rule.
findings.fix: Require Run and its fixtures to arrange deferred cleanup immediately for every non-nil plaintext/key buffer, before checking errors or making assertions, including buffers received with errors or late cancellation results. Add a deliberately violating source and a controlled failing assertion/cancellation path that prove the harness clears those buffers without printing their contents.

findings.summary: Same-node replacement bypasses #72's capacity admission and leaves capacity observations unbound to the store that reported them.
findings.evidence: 61/design.md:73-77 describes ReplaceReplicaStore as a chunk/header/ref CAS with no capacity report, Room check or ledger change. Reviewed 72/design.md Charging and release and capacity-contracts.md charge every new move destination under a ledger compare, retain lost/released copies until exact cleanup, and expose node-keyed reports without store UUID. A replacement can therefore allocate an additional full copy without its charge; changing observed_store_uuid at 61/design.md:25-28 also leaves an old store's alive/capacity report eligible for the new store. A differently sized replacement can inherit the old disk's admission budget.
findings.fix: Define the replacement transaction's Room/ledger/charge semantics, preserving conservative charges for inaccessible old refs and snapshot multiplicity when #51 is active. Bind reports and report acceptance to the observed UUID/generation, invalidate old-store reports atomically on identity change, and reject delayed old-store heartbeats. State last-landing hooks for #72 rather than introducing a second capacity authority. Test replacement versus create/move/InitCapacity/release races and the larger-old/smaller-new disk case on both backends.

findings.summary: The simulator proof does not yet define executable checks and caught mutants for all newly introduced recovery rules.
findings.evidence: 61/design.md:152-165 groups broad scenarios and explicitly names only identity_alias and bootstrap-old-token, then says every identity rule will get a check/bypass. Actual ReplicaCore::handle (replica.rs:173-199) takes Hello straight to fencing, the simulator precreates chunks (sim/mod.rs:395-401), and crash retains durable state (:1107-1121). There is no specified pure bootstrap authorization/fence-completion state or independently checked oracle for the new same-node replacement/full-resync/join transition. An identity-alias counterexample does not demonstrate rejection of dirty-only replacement, early UUID binding/join or replayed authorization after an epoch/ref change.
findings.fix: Give the sans-I/O bootstrap and replacement transitions concrete events/state/actions, including authorization completion, durable-fence completion, cancellation and chunk roles. Map each new safety rule to its independent simulator assertion, a named violating mutation, and the bounded scenario that must catch it. At minimum separate identity/ack/lease isolation, current-authority bootstrap, full-range-before-join, current-epoch/version replacement and no-authoritative-source refusal. Name real production adapter tests for both accepted remote and synthetic local Hello paths, delayed callbacks, fast-read admission/completion and restart boundaries.

findings.summary: The approved enrollment policy has no implementable migration/activation API or durable concurrency contract.
findings.evidence: 61/design.md:100-112 specifies administrator enroll-store, CAS batch cursors, inventory generation and activation, but Files and contracts names no enrollment RPC, persistent schema/keys, request/response, authorization/error rules, batch bound or activation linearization condition. Current meta/service/auth.go only recognizes enumerated RPCs, while current KV supplies ordinary Get/List/Txn APIs. The conceptual maintenance stop does not define how a resumed migration distinguishes inventories or proves every assignment/fence/release/tombstone was converted before identity-required mode resumes. The historical Q1 decision settles provenance policy, not these missing mechanisms.
findings.fix: Define the administrator-only enrollment and activation contracts with bounded batches, exact inventory/operation identity, conditional revisions, durable cursor/idempotency, conflict and lost-reply behavior, quarantine representation, and the complete activation predicate. Explain how interrupted migration and concurrent/new io registration are handled under the maintenance barrier. Add real memory/etcd restart/concurrency and auth-matrix tests; preserve the historical administrator-evidence decision without claiming these new details were already approved.

findings.summary: The bootstrap grant does not define how an already-open session acquires or enforces authority for a later move/replacement.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/61/design.md:44–56, 79–85, 130–137 authorize the Hello's requested chunk set once and cache only in that session. Actual replica/mod.rs:346–353 creates a missing chunk on BeginResync; the target can add a new move destination on an existing node/volume session. A session established before that assignment has no matching SessionAssignment, and the design never specifies per-request grant enforcement or a transition to acquire its new role.
findings.fix: Persist the authorized chunk/ref/role/operation set in the accepted session and check it before every creation or reconstruction operation. Define a bounded control-path reauthorization or explicit new-Hello transition when moves add chunks/roles, including operation changes, session supersession, and delayed answers. Do not add metadata calls to ordinary I/O. Test a session predating the move, an ungranted BeginResync, and a stale replacement operation before any store mutation.

findings.summary: The new replica-gate exceeds the concrete release transaction limit.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/61/design.md:59–64 requires an extra atomically bumped gate on release mutations. The current #13 design.md:105–122 permits 118 chunk comparisons plus header and #72 ledger comparisons, exactly 120. Adding the gate makes 121, refused by meta/kv/etcd.go:91–92. #13's sweep concretely emits batches of 118. findings.summary: Deployment surge can mint two global disruption credits for one observation.

Concurrent A/B slot evictions both succeed, and their permit evictions can complete both unsafe drains. Re-reading observedGeneration does not make pod count equal distinct-node count. findings.summary: The guard has no concrete composition with the now-canonical exact-store membership and paged-volume contracts.

TCP may execute receive/softirq work outside the endpoint threads (for example ksoftirqd), and async I/O helpers may run elsewhere. Thread CPU clocks and perf attached only to those TIDs exclude that work rather than putting it in the unknown bucket. In contrast memory streams remove kernel processing. The resulting paired CPU difference can therefore omit precisely the displaced work while being reported as total endpoint/transport CPU.
findings.fix: Define the accounting boundary explicitly: retain endpoint-thread CPU as a labeled partial metric, record helper threads and a bounded system/CPU-scoped kernel/background observation for local trials, and treat unattributable off-thread work as unknown. Only present a transport-total CPU difference when its accounting coverage is qualified; otherwise report the endpoint-only difference and an inconclusive kernel/total saving. Do not add overlapping thread and system counters. Add an analysis fixture with nonzero off-thread network work and one with unavailable system profiling, verifying neither silently becomes zero or a qualified total.

Without a specific benchmark-only lifecycle, repeated fixtures can overlap teardown or leave listeners/tasks alive while later trials start, violating the stated isolation and contaminating counters.

An explicitly scoped dev-only lifecycle mechanism is another option if it leaves product behavior unchanged. Add a fixture test proving no owned process/listener remains after timeout and repeated trials do not overlap.

findings.summary: Bounded routing needs an event-capacity and terminal-delivery rule that remains nonblocking under the engine lock.

Current ublk.rs:605–615 ignores try_send failure and removes the waiter for Done. One legitimate depth-one read crossing two remote chunk pieces can generate Piece, Piece, Done before its consumer runs (engine.rs:1889–1900 emits each direct-read Piece; sub_done then emits Done). A request-count bound alone is not an event bound. Converting these channels to bounded queues without a stated mailbox/credit policy can discard Done after route removal, hang the request and exhaust the binding; blocking on capacity while holding the engine lock can deadlock the read/stop path.

Reserve capacity before engine admission or retain terminal state separately; never remove a live route before its terminal result is durably owned by the mailbox. State full/closed behavior explicitly (safe binding failure is acceptable, silent event loss is not), preserving memory and local-I/O ownership during stop. Add a paused-consumer depth-one multi-piece read fixture, saturated/closed mailbox and stop race fixtures proving terminal delivery or explicit fail-closed completion without an engine-lock wait.

findings.summary: The frontend batch lifetime contract does not define how unwinding is stopped before pending kernel buffers are destroyed.

Current local_read and fast_read_copy in ublk.rs:1293–1341,1638–1694 publish raw-buffer SQEs while building pending Vecs. Pinned libublk0.4.8 io.rs:2231–2233 unwraps submission, uring_async.rs:546–570 eagerly pushes SQEs before returning the future, and UblkUringOpFuture (uring_async.rs:26–90) has no draining Drop. Ordinary future/Vec ownership therefore does not keep a request buffer alive when its task unwinds or is dropped with SQEs outstanding. #85 explicitly adds armed abort-on-unwind protection to UringDevice; that separate device ring does not protect the ublk queue ring, and the current flaminio-io daemon has no existing abort/exit path to invoke here.
findings.fix: Define the queue-local batch ownership mechanism explicitly: prepare lengths/buffers/bookkeeping before the first publication, arm a fail-stop-on-unwind/drop guard before any SQE can be published, and retain it through every completion and ownership-releasing cleanup. Its guard must execute before borrowed buffers/plans/tasks can be destroyed, with partial publication or unprovable drain terminating the process without unwinding those owners. Ordinary cancellation/error must drain before release. This can follow #85’s principle without adding an external protocol or changing the settled thin-signature prototype. Add subprocess/injected-backend fixtures for panic after first publication, partial setup, task cancellation and panic during completion/cleanup; prove fail-stop occurs before a tracked pending backing allocation is released, using an independent backing reference so the test never creates dangling kernel memory.

At dependency 67862ad667ac3121b453c9227cef1e8ec5248138, #83 spec S1 and design.md:19-42 require physical-boottime-v1 and explicitly refuse existing lab VMs; a qualification run cannot make these VMs supported. #84 design.md:224-227 already records the compatible before-#83/after-#83 distinction. Thus this plan has no executable success path under its own stated composed prerequisite.
findings.fix: Add an explicit whoever-lands-second composition in #67 only: before #83 lands, any VM evidence is limited to the old supported/test baseline and cannot certify physical clock admission; after #83 lands, gateway-up/test on these VMs refuses before publication/mutation, and the two-node success/restart qualification runs on two admitted physical workload hosts. Preserve one manually provisioned node-pinned gateway and no node-loss failover. State what physical and minimum-kernel #84 evidence is actually required rather than imply VM checks satisfy it. Add fake preflight fixtures for excluded VM refusal and admitted two-node setup, and label the future real evidence by host/profile.

findings.summary: The plan omits the host NFS-client dependency needed for the static NFS PV to mount.
findings.evidence: intent.md:61-68 explicitly observes that lab VMs lack mount.nfs and that their kernel NFS-client support is unverified. scripts/guest/provision.sh:10 installs neither nfs-common nor equivalent client tooling. design.md:63-69 uses an in-tree NFS PV, and :103-110/:130-151 define setup/files/tests without any host-client installation or fail-closed helper/module preflight. Building a Ganesha/tunnel image under scripts/dev does not supply the kubelet host mount namespace. Official Kubernetes source pkg/volume/nfs/nfs.go:221-227 passes type nfs to the host mounter (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/v1.34.0/pkg/volume/nfs/nfs.go). A normal provisioned lab node therefore cannot perform the promised consumer mount.
findings.fix: Specify the supported host NFSv4.1 client package/helper and kernel capability prerequisites on both consumer nodes. Either add explicit lab provisioning changes (including scripts/guest/provision.sh in the files list), or document an operator-installed prerequisite and make up/test refuse before creating/publicizing resources when the actual kubelet host helper or kernel client is absent. Record client versions in qualification and add missing-helper/missing-client-support fixtures plus the future real mount through each node-local proxy.

findings.summary: The stable-ACK qualification needs an ordering/error oracle beyond process-kill checksum survival.
findings.evidence: design.md:39-42 requires durable shutdown-independent ordering, but its concrete S2 evidence at :143 and Lab :156-158 is stable-write/COMMIT/fsync plus SIGKILL and byte verification. Killing Ganesha on the same node does not discard the backing filesystem kernel page cache; an erroneous server that calls pwritev then returns stable success before fsync can pass that restart/checksum test. Existing #84 tests establish durability of completed block writes, not that Ganesha waited for its filesystem sync before an NFS stable reply. Official Ganesha VFS file.c:1322-1340 and :1570-1614 show the actual boundary: pwritev, conditional fsync before done_cb for stable WRITE, and fsync status for COMMIT (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nfs-ganesha/nfs-ganesha/next/src/FSAL/FSAL_VFS/file.c). The draft needs a concrete fixture that fails when this required ordering is omitted.
findings.fix: Extend the accepted pinned-release qualification with observed filesystem-sync-to-NFS-reply ordering and deterministic delayed/failed sync cases for both stable WRITE and COMMIT. For example, gate the selected release’s actual fsync/fdatasync boundary and show no stable-success reply until successful completion; return an injected sync error and assert no stable-success reply. Include a negative candidate/fixture that skips the wait so the oracle demonstrably fails. Retain SIGKILL/reclaim tests and #84 block conformance; no new replica rule, node-loss test or shared-lab execution is required for this plan review.

findings.summary: Teardown needs a consumer-withdrawal barrier before checking that mounts are gone.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/67/design.md:113-117 checks for live consumer pods/mounts and then removes TLS/proxies/server, but never withdraws the still-bound consumer claim or prevents new use of it. Under spec.md Tenant/S4, an ordinary unprivileged pod creator in the authorized consumer namespace can create another allowed PVC-using Pod after that check; Restricted admission explicitly allows persistentVolumeClaim volumes (Kubernetes Pod Security Standards, https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/). Its kubelet mount can race proxy unmount/removal or a later reuse of the per-export port. UID ownership checks protect which objects are deleted but do not serialize this new mount against down, so S7 teardown cannot prove consumers have stopped.
findings.fix: Define a minimal durable withdrawal/quiescence protocol before the no-consumer check, for example remove the exact owned consumer-claim UID from usable service and wait for claim protection plus existing and in-flight node mounts to retire, or use an equally concrete admission barrier. Keep the barrier effective across interruption/resume and refuse proxy/port/server retirement while any old consumer operation remains ambiguous. Reuse of names/ports must not authorize an old mount against a replacement export. Add fake/API/node fixtures creating a new Pod and delaying a mount between the initial check and removal, plus interrupted/resumed withdrawal and claim/port replacement. Preserve backing data and the existing no-force-unmount rule.

findings.summary: The new tenant-driven server and tunnel processes lack a finite resource-containment profile and pressure qualification.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/67/design.md:94-101 qualifies capabilities/seccomp but specifies no CPU/memory/pid/fd or connection/handshake/buffering limits for Ganesha, its pod tunnel or the host node proxies. Contracts at :121-127 and tests at :142-148 likewise omit pressure/exhaustion behavior. Authorized unprivileged consumers can generate many opens/locks and concurrent filesystem operations; a network peer reaching the TLS listener can also occupy pre-authentication work. Neither root squash nor mTLS bounds that work. Ganesha documents independent RPC_Max_Connections, RPC_Ioq_ThrdMax, DRC and send/receive-buffer controls (https://github.com/nfs-ganesha/nfs-ganesha/blob/next/src/doc/man/ganesha-core-config.rst), but this plan does not select/qualify even an overall containment boundary. An unconstrained gateway or host proxy can exhaust resources shared with the storage node, beyond the export trust boundary.
findings.fix: Add a bounded per-export qualification profile using ordinary container/service CPU, memory, task/fd controls and supported server/tunnel connection, handshake and buffer limits, with explicit overload/timeout/restart semantics preserving stable-write and recovery rules. Exact version-specific values may remain in the approved qualification artifact, but finite budget categories, host-proxy containment and pass criteria must be required now. Add future slow/failed TLS handshake and concurrent NFS open/request pressure fixtures proving bounded ownership/cleanup and safe recovery after containment kills. This does not require filesystem quotas, a custom transport-memory proof or a new replication protocol.

rounds.resolution: R1-C1: explicit before/after #83 VM/physical host qualification matrix. R1-C2: operator-installed host NFS client/helper and fail-closed actual kubelet preflight. SEC67-R1-01: durable per-export host mount-helper gate seals delayed calls, retains bounded invocation ownership and requires both-node/API quiescence before endpoint retirement. SEC67-R1-02: finite ordinary server/tunnel/host-proxy containment and pressure/restart qualification. findings.summary: A fresh Serving lifetime must distinguish delayed helper calls from a previously retired consumer of the same export.
findings.evidence: withdrawal-contract.md:9-24 gates only (loopback address, port, /flaminio/<persistent export UUID>) and records the current consumer PVC UID internally; :59-64 releases the endpoint after retirement and permits replacement consumers with a new PVC UID. A kubelet mount operation paused before entering this dispatcher owns no invocation token or mount yet. It can arrive after down seals/retires and a later up reuses that same export/port for a new claim. It then sees fresh Serving and identical source/options; the old PVC UID is not an incoming credential the dispatcher can compare. Official Kubernetes v1.34 NFS plugin nfs.go:221-227 sends only server:exportPath, target and mount options to the host mounter, and nestedpendingoperations.go:167-175 runs saved mount work asynchronously; operation_generator.go:395-416,515-523 uses its captured VolumeSpec/Pod. API absence and the current mount/token inventory therefore do not establish that every not-yet-entered helper call has vanished. Persistent export UUID alone does not fence a replacement consumer lifetime.
findings.fix: Bind each new consumer/Serving lifetime to a fresh mount-admission generation carried in the actual immutable PV source or an endpoint tuple that is never reused for that lifetime, and reject old generations before real-helper launch. Keep persistent NFS filesystem/export identity separately for same-lifetime process restart and data retention. Define retained/rejected stale-source behavior so an old owned source never falls through to the unrelated-NFS delegation path; no new CSI controller is needed. Add a fixture pausing an old cached kubelet operation before dispatcher entry, completing down and opening a new claim for the same backing export, then releasing the old call: it must be refused while a new-generation call succeeds. Include interrupted retirement/reopening and name/port reuse.

rounds.resolution: SEC67-R2-01: immutable PV source now carries actual consumer PVC UID alongside permanent export UUID, with Pending-PVC UID acquisition/Preparing/binding/Serving order. Added delayed-before-dispatch/reopen and partial-publication fixtures. Historical decision/ADR prefixes preserved; 23 links and staged whitespace checked; no runtime/helper/API/server/lab tests. findings.summary: Define an independent partial-update history/oracle; changing only the register's initial value cannot check S4.
findings.evidence: design.md:58–61 represents a smaller client update as read/merge/write, but :139–144 specifies only adding an initial value to check_register and lists partial-update zero-fill as a caught mutation. Actual src/sim/mod.rs:322–328 records write: Option<Value>; check_block (:1370–1407) converts it directly to CKind::Write(v). src/sim/check.rs:23–25/113–116 supports only whole-value replacement, and types.rs defines Value=u64. Recording the target's merged value as that replacement would make a broken merge the expected client write: subsequent reads returning its zero-filled remainder remain linearizable. There is no concrete partial operand/range representation or independent expected-state transition in this plan, so the promised S4 safety mutation has no defined independent oracle.
findings.fix: Specify a bounded model block value and an original client partial-update input (mask/offset/length and replacement bytes/lanes), retain that input in HistOp, and define an independent checker transition that applies it to its own prior register state. Do not derive the expected full value from the implementation's read/merge result. Name deterministic concurrent partial/full-write and nonzero-neighbor cases and a zero-fill mutant that this oracle catches. If using an independent literal/reference expectation instead, specify how it remains correct under the modeled overlapping histories.

findings.summary: The model-only increment needs a compile-safe boundary for its new shared core contracts.
findings.evidence: design.md:51–53 introduces core FetchBase outputs/on_fetch, :70 adds HydrateIfRemote, and :35–44 adds typed digest/range/copy contracts; :121–125 changes flaminio-repl::{msg,target,replica} while expressly excluding node/net changes. In the actual workspace these are shared production types: flaminio-node/src/engine.rs:2361–2411 exhaustively translates Request<Payload> to existing Frame variants; replica/mod.rs:355–444 exhaustively handles ReplicaCore Action, and :954–962 exhaustively translates Response. The current simulator's Replica also exhaustively handles Action (replica.rs:345 onward). Adding the planned variants to those shared enums without adapter changes breaks the workspace build; silently projecting them onto ordinary writes/holes would defeat the approved model-only boundary. The plan does not select an isolated API/gating strategy or explicit rejecting adapter changes.
findings.fix: Choose and document a compiling delivery boundary: e.g. a separate hydration model/core facade with unchanged existing runtime enums, or explicit minimal fail-closed runtime adapter arms/feature admission that cannot emit or accept hydration on the existing wire. List the affected adapter files if that option is chosen. Specify workspace compilation of ordinary/default consumers plus simulator coverage of the hydration path. Keep actual store/wire/worker implementation in the already deferred runtime stages.

findings.summary: The new base-pin admission/lifetime safety rule has no independent model assertion or caught mutation.
findings.evidence: spec.md S9 (lines67-70) requires the pinned base to remain retained until completion or deletion; S10 (lines72-75) requires every new safety rule to have a caught mutation. design.md:100-104 introduces a durable pin before Hydrating exposure and permits release only after Complete/deletion commits. However its concrete independent checks at :139-144 cover initial-value linearizability, acknowledged state agreement and post-Complete repository events; the nine named mutations do not omit initial pin acquisition or release a pin early. In the explicitly grow-only/no-GC repository, removing a pin need not change any data, read result, presence state or post-Complete fetch event, so all of those oracles can still pass while S9 is violated. The existing simulator check path (sim/mod.rs:1345-1407 and sim/check.rs:32-61) has no repository/pin oracle to supply this implicitly. The mapped #52 design similarly treats its own reader-pin closure as an independent checker and catches premature_pin_release; that is a distinct grant/source lifecycle and does not establish #68 destination-base pin coverage.
findings.fix: Define the modeled base-pin state and an independent per-transition assertion relating the immutable requested destination-incarnation/base identity to pin admission and terminal commits: no Hydrating exposure without its exact live pin, and no pin release before that incarnation’s Complete or deletion commit. Add deterministic/seeded cases for crash/retry, failed/lost completion and deletion/recreation, with at least omit-initial-pin and early-release mutations that each fail that assertion on a clean-passing scenario. Keep this in the protocol/model increment; no runtime repository collector, credential protocol, bucket mutation or wire-format implementation is required.

findings.summary: Specify the exact metadata-server role/URI predicate and its configuration before trusting the status response.
findings.evidence: design.md:60-64 retains CA/hostname verification and says to verify server identity/trust domain through existing PKI helpers, but supplies only --trust-domain/--timeout and no expected metadata-server identity or role predicate. Actual pkg/pki/pki.go:301-314 ClientConfig checks the configured CA/hostname through TLS but installs no URI verifier; PeerIdentity at :244-260 checks a single parsed URI and trust domain, accepting any recognized node/admin role. A same-CA ServerAuth certificate for another component with the endpoint hostname/IP is therefore not excluded by the named helpers. The lab issues role certificates on shared node IPs (scripts/lab.sh:582-583), and generic CA tooling can issue ServerAuth for a validated identity. A node/io or admin server must not substitute a fabricated healthy view for the metadata service. Current #91 security-contract.md:45-49 already states the intended exact node/<configured-server-node>/meta predicate; #71 observer hostname isolation is narrower and does not supply it.
findings.fix: Define explicit configured expected metadata server node/URI (or a finite exact allowlist for configured endpoints), and require exactly one URI SAN in the configured trust domain with node and component=meta matching that endpoint, in addition to normal CA/hostname/EKU checks. State where the predicate runs before any response is trusted and reject missing/mismatched configuration without admin/insecure fallback. Reuse shared PKI helpers with a caller-specific predicate rather than granting generic same-domain trust. Add actual TLS fixtures with correct CA and endpoint hostname but wrong component/node/admin/reader URI, plus the exact valid metadata URI; wrong-role peers must fail before any status RPC result is accepted.

findings.summary: Turn the 64MiB collection/encoding requirement into a concrete before-allocation typed-data and output budget.
findings.evidence: design.md:44-48 names counts, existing per-RPC receive bound and post-response protobuf validation; :125-127 says pre-allocation bounds are needed but does not define their implementation. It gives no pre-Unmarshal cardinality admission, retained/temporary/encoded accounting or bounded encoder. Actual pinned grpc1.85.0 rpc_util.go:1051-1065 checks received/decompressed bytes then calls codec.Unmarshal; encoding/proto/proto.go:85-96 materializes input and calls proto.Unmarshal. Pinned protobuf1.36.12 internal/impl/codec_field.go:438-455 allocates a child and appends it for every repeated message before Collect can inspect its count. ListNodesResponse.nodes and ListTombstonesResponse.tombstones are repeated pointers (meta.pb.go:407-412,1137-1142): a valid-size stream of two-byte empty message entries can allocate millions of child objects while remaining within the 4MiB wire cap. Likewise a normal unbounded json.Marshal can allocate its complete escaped output before a 64MiB check. Thus the concrete design does not yet enforce S5 at the boundary it explicitly requires. #91 reader-contract.md:98-119 demonstrates compatible guard-local preflight/application credits, but its guard-only destination set excludes status tombstone responses and is not adopted here.
findings.fix: Specify the smallest concrete status-local or shared bounded decode/collection/encoding contract: preflight supported protobuf field/cardinality/string/nesting bounds before typed construction, reserve finite application credits before RPC/append, account retained views and temporary/encoded output without overlap/double-counting, and encode to a bounded owned result before stdout publication. Keep stock gRPC receive/header/client limits and distinguish application data credits from private Go/gRPC heap ownership; no whole-library 64MiB proof, fork, daemon cgroup or admission-guard restart machinery is required. Reuse the relevant #90 profiles/#91 preflight principle through an explicit whoever-lands-second helper where useful, preserving CLI omission semantics. Add repeated-empty-message, many small records, maximal escaping/encoding expansion, concurrent four-call budget, decode failure/cancellation and output-over-limit fixtures that prove refusal before excess typed/retained/output allocation and no stdout success.

findings.summary: INITIAL creation authority has no defined issuance/consumption transition distinguishing first bootstrap from earned membership.
findings.evidence: 90/core-design.md:24-25,35-47 allows INITIAL to create and requires MEMBER to exist, but defines INITIAL only by the #76 initial-placement operation. 90/contracts.md:45-79 has no pending-initial/earned field or completion transaction. Actual meta/domain/domain.go:199-207 places every new replica in the ISR before any Hello; reviewed #76 design.md:24,48-59 retains create_operation and its immutable plan after publication, attach and later mutation. Consequently those same metadata fields describe both a never-materialized initial copy and an earned copy on a later attach. The grant algorithm cannot select the stated roles or establish when INITIAL can no longer be reissued. No INITIAL replay/consumption check or caught mutant appears in the proof table.
findings.fix: Define authoritative bounded initial-materialization state and the exact transition from creation permission to earned source/ack/lease authority, including completion CAS/durable evidence and partial-bootstrap crash/takeover behavior. Specify role selection at Open/Page/Finish and session transition after completion; add an independent simulator assertion/caught INITIAL-replay mutant plus actual first attach, partial creation restart, lost completion reply and post-earned missing-chunk refusal tests.

findings.summary: Cleanup has neither a stored-tombstone byte bound nor a bounded ListTombstones response path.
findings.evidence: 90/contracts.md:90-106 stores the entire volume union of placed/moving/released/fenced/claimed refs and per-ref charges in one tombstone and adds refs/pending_refs/confirmed_refs to each reply. Per-chunk release and 16-fence limits do not bound the union to a small record; distinct old UUIDs are deliberately not deduplicated by node. 90/budgets.md:9-42 proves only Volume responses; :46-56 also promises exact deletion for paged legacy volumes up to65536 chunks. No tombstone record bytes, list count/bytes, paging cursor or bounded scan is specified. Actual service.go:584-614 lists the entire tombstone prefix and returns every matching tombstone; meta.proto:182-184 has one unpaged repeated result. Many ordinary pending deletions exceed the unchanged4MiB receive limit, and a large exact-ref union can exceed the backend request/value envelope even when its Volume view has a paged path. 90/migration.md:98-106 also assumes a tombstone fits one16KiB item/binding.
findings.fix: Define bounded persistent tombstone roots/ref-charge pages and atomic deletion/confirmation progress, or another exact representation whose worst stored transaction fits the real backend byte limit. Add bounded count-and-byte ListTombstones paging (including one large tombstone), stable incarnation/revision semantics, bounded backend scans and sweep continuation; compose enrollment with the same pages. Publish exact storage/transport envelopes and both-backend plus real Go/Rust boundary/+1 fixtures, many pending volumes and maximal legacy union cases without raising receive limits.

findings.summary: Mandatory replica-gate puts disable #76 delete-only recovery under etcd NOSPACE.
findings.evidence: 90/contracts.md:138-149 requires a compared/incremented gate on creation abort and public cleanup, deletion chunk cleanup and final deletion, with no helper exception. 90/budgets.md:175-181 requires the gate write in other deletion transactions and explicitly adds it to post-header cleanup. Reviewed #76 design.md:80-112 deliberately makes unpublished header rollback, root revocation and orphan plan/public-chunk cleanup delete-only: etcd3.7 rejects any transaction containing a Put while NOSPACE is raised (its source fact is design.md:11-12). Adding the proposed gate Put makes those recovery operations fail precisely when they are needed to reclaim space.
findings.fix: Compose an explicit delete-only exception for proof-scoped unpublished rollback/revocation/orphan reclamation, retaining identity-mode and exact root/header/key revision comparisons. Explain why absent/unpublished header plus those irreversible fences makes a gate increment unnecessary for grant freshness, or supply a different concrete NOSPACE-safe fencing mechanism. Keep all genuinely live authority changes gated. Update transaction tables and add real-etcd NOSPACE rollback/root-GC/public-and-private-orphan tests, with late publication/authorization/recreation schedules and a caught safety mutant for the exception.

findings.summary: INITIAL creation has no durable pending-to-earned transition, so first bootstrap and forbidden recreation are not distinguishable.
findings.evidence: 90/core-design.md:24-25,35-44,93-95 authorizes INITIAL by the #76 create operation, permits allocation, and requires earned membership for ordinary acknowledgements/source/lease credit. 90/design.md:48-49 says the created copy stays unearned until reconstruction/join, but no INITIAL completion event, stored state, RPC/CAS, or initial join is defined. findings.summary: Exact-ref tombstones and their lists have no aggregate storage/response envelope or bounded migration representation.
findings.evidence: 90/contracts.md:90-106 unions every chunk replica/move/released ref and fence holder into one tombstone with refs, pending_refs and confirmed_refs plus per-UUID charges. UUID changes prevent the former node deduplication from bounding that union. 90/budgets.md:26-42 bounds Volume responses only; :46-97 pages oversized legacy Volumes only. Actual meta/service/service.go:584-614 ListTombstones scans and returns every matching full tombstone, with no page/byte cap. Even legal new RF1/N2955 volumes can retain two distinct old UUID releases per chunk, yielding about 5911 refs and roughly 2 MiB in the two full protobuf ref projections per tombstone with maximal node names; three tombstones pending for the same current ref exceed 4 MiB. The explicitly supported N65536 legacy path can exceed that in one tombstone. 90/migration.md:53-59,98-106,131-144 nevertheless requires each whole tombstone inventory/binding item <=16 KiB and to fit one <=120-key coupled transaction; a legal large tombstone cannot satisfy that representation. Raising receive limits would violate the preserved #80 contract.
findings.fix: Give exact cleanup its own bounded persisted representation and list/page/confirmation contract, covering total per-volume ref/charge multiplicity, backend request/value limits, aggregate RPC bytes and stable incarnation/revision pagination. Adapt deletion publication, sweep/admin clients, both-backend migration inventory/conversion and capacity accounting so every admitted new/paged-legacy volume remains deletable without truncating refs or dropping charges. Specify numerical caps and boundary/+1 real transport/backend fixtures, including many tombstones for one node and repeated same-node UUID replacements. Keep dependencies read-only; assign the composition hooks to #90.

findings.summary: Enrollment cannot correct an already processed item after changed observations or failed verification.
findings.evidence: 90/migration.md:131-144 accepts only the next inventory positions, or an identical retry of the latest batch ID; it has no amendment/rebind API. :145-157 begins verification only after enroll_cursor==inventory_count, then sends a failed scan back to ENROLLING with a cursor invalidated and requires explicit correction. :164-169 also allows changed UUID observations after binding and requires quarantine/review before VERIFYING. The contracts specify neither a rewind/revision-safe rewrite of an already converted item nor an operation that records that quarantine and updates coupled refs/charges/evidence. Advancing the enrollment cursor to the end therefore removes the only defined way to repair the affected item, while a replacement enrollment job is explicitly forbidden.
findings.fix: Define a bounded conditional correction/rebind-or-quarantine operation for already inventoried/converted items, or an exact durable rewind protocol, including expected original/current hashes, evidence/observation revisions, coupled-key updates, capacity conservation, counter changes, idempotence and invalidation/restart of verification digests. Keep READY immutable. Test changed observation after binding and verification failure after the final batch through correction, restart, lost reply and successful re-verification/activation on both backends.

findings.summary: Node precommit enrollment has no authenticated API-server client boundary and permits irreversible forged allocations.
findings.evidence: 91/security-contract.md:48-61 establishes server TLS but no required client certificate, authenticated peer identity, or API-server admission plugin credential configuration; its assertion that fake reviews must pass actual-object checks is false for the new precommit CREATE path. 91/admission-contract.md:37-48,75-89 allocates a lifetime-counted enrollment and creates an anchor for a request Node UID before that Node exists, retains failed creates indefinitely, and has no runtime reclamation. A caller reaching 9443 can forge Node CREATE reviews with fresh syntactically valid names/UIDs, exhaust all4096 allocations and block legitimate node creation without Kubernetes Node-create permission. Per-process serialization/body/network bounds slow this attack but do not authenticate it. The exact pinned resolver defaults to anonymous when no webhook auth kubeconfig entry matches: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.36.5/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/webhook/authentication.go#L127-L205 . This also violates AGENTS.md every-connection-mTLS principle.
findings.fix: Specify an installable pinned k3s/API-server client-authentication configuration for both admission plugins, service-DNS credential matching, dedicated client credential trust and exact peer identity/EKU validation on the guard, HA and rotation behavior, and fail-closed missing/mismatched credentials. Authenticate before accepting/decoding actionable review state or allocating resources. Keep API re-reads as object validation rather than client authentication. Add actual pinned API fixtures for successful authenticated Node enrollment/eviction, unauthenticated and wrong-role forged Node CREATE rejection with zero allocation/state changes, certificate rotation, and absence of credential configuration. Do not leave the mechanism behind a qualification/approval gate.

findings.summary: The mandatory anchors on nonstorage Nodes have no satisfiable normal slot recovery path.
findings.evidence: 91/design.md:17-19 and admission-contract.md:75-81 deliberately anchor every Node, including unlabeled/nonstorage nodes; design.md:86 explicitly places the serving Deployment on preexisting nonstorage management nodes. admission-contract.md:67-70 requires every terminal/image/repair replacement to reserve the global slot, while :130-141 releases only after the same Node has a live metadata store and full relevant earned ISR. A genuine Kubernetes-only worker/management node has no store_uuid/generation or metadata Node record by definition, so an admitted drain/ordinary anchor refresh on it cannot satisfy recovery even after uncordon and a healthy Ready replacement. Alternatively treating its absent mapping as Unknown prevents the refresh/drain in the first place. This is a normal installation composition case, not privileged bypass or missing human approval; one such slot blocks subsequent storage maintenance cluster-wide.
findings.fix: Define explicit storage-backed and proven nonstorage candidate/recovery cases while preserving coverage of every Node before it could become storage. For a nonstorage Node, state the complete fresh service/Kubernetes absence/reference predicates that substitute for the nonexistent live-store/ISR requirement, how transition to storage during admission/recovery is detected conservatively, and when its slot can be released. Never classify a missing/dead formerly registered storage node as harmless nonstorage. Add real-API plus actual-reader fixtures for a healthy Kubernetes-only worker anchor terminal/image refresh and drain/uncordon/release followed by a storage drain, and for metadata registration/references appearing during that path, metadata read failure and formerly-storage Node absence.

findings.summary: The reducer requires a unique metadata-node to Kubernetes-UID mapping but never defines its source or exact matching rule.
findings.evidence: 91/spec.md Terms defines Node identity as UID/name mapped to metadata node ID, and reader-contract.md:107-115 requires a unique enrolled Kubernetes UID mapping, external exclusivity and Unknown on a conflicting mapping. However admission-contract.md:37-39 persists only Kubernetes name/UID and anchor identity; no metadata ID binding, label field or mapping algorithm is specified, and the command exposes only external-node IDs. Actual api/proto/flaminio/meta/v1/meta.proto Node carries id/address/labels but no Kubernetes UID; #90 adds store UUID/generation, not this association. Existing deployment uses --node-id=$(NODE_NAME) (deploy/csi/driver.yaml:112-124) and control/csi/topology.go:59 calls NodeLabels with that nodeID, which provides a workable exact-name convention but is not made normative by #91. Equality, hostname/address inference and caller labels have different collision/recreation behavior at precisely the candidate-exclusion trust boundary.
findings.fix: State one concrete read-only mapping protocol, preferably the existing exact metadataID==Node.metadata.name convention if that is the intended supported profile, including grammar/length handling, durable enrollment comparison, external-ID collision rules and same-name/new-UID refusal. If aliases are supported, specify their trusted installation/configuration authority and immutable binding rather than inferring from addresses or untrusted labels. Add reducer/real-reader tests for the valid mapping, differently named IDs, duplicate/conflicting aliases, external collision and same-name UID replacement. Keep this composition owned by #91 and do not reopen dependencies.

findings.summary: The webhook authenticates its server but accepts unauthenticated callers that can allocate permanent enrollment state.
findings.evidence: security-contract.md:48-61 supplies only the serving leaf/key and explicitly treats fake reviews as at worst consuming a slot. admission-contract.md:75-89 instead accepts a precommit Node UID which cannot yet be checked against a live Node, creates a finalizer-bearing nodeName-bound Pod and nonreclaimable Staging enrollment, and consumes the lifetime4096 counter. A caller reaching9443 can forge successive CREATE reviews with syntactically valid nonexistent UIDs, consume all allocations, and plant blocking Staging anchors on an existing node. Actual-object rereads do not authenticate this precommit request. No API-server client credential, listener client-CA/identity rule or k3s admission-plugin credential configuration is specified. Pinned Kubernetes authentication.go:130-132,148-150,204-205 uses anonymous webhook client configuration when no matching credentials are installed; caBundle authenticates the opposite direction. Source: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.36.5/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/webhook/authentication.go .
findings.fix: Specify and provision authenticated API-server-to-webhook TLS for every pinned control-plane instance and both admission plugins, including exact credential selection, trust/identity verification, rotation and fail-closed startup. Authenticate before parsing or durable side effects; network policy and AdmissionReview fields remain insufficient. Add real transport fixtures proving no-client/wrong-client/expired-client and forged/replayed direct reviews cannot allocate enrollments, create anchors or reserve a slot, while the actual API server can perform all three paths.

findings.summary: An ordinary kubelet re-registration can create a permanent uncommitted anchor that blocks its node drain.
findings.evidence: admission-contract.md:75-89 allocates a new UID-owned anchor for every validating Node CREATE and retains Staging until that exact UID has been observed and later deleted; :109-110 rejects its eviction unless its enrollment committed. Kubernetes generic store assigns the new UID and runs createValidation before Storage.Create checks the existing key (store.go:445-490). Pinned kubelet_node_status.go:84-104 starts registration with Nodes().Create even when the name already exists, then handles AlreadyExists by reading/reconciling the existing Node. A routine kubelet restart therefore generates a different never-committed UID, leaves its Staging anchor bound to the real existing nodeName, and later drain encounters a Pod whose NodeUID can never match. This is more than the documented lifetime-counter saturation cost. Sources: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.36.5/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/registry/generic/registry/store.go#L445-L490 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.36.5/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_node_status.go#L84-L104 .
findings.fix: Handle already-existing Node names and overlapping creates before allocating new permanent staging state, preserving the pinned kubelet AlreadyExists/reconciliation behavior without allowing an uncovered create to commit. Define the durable same-name contention/error branch and its response semantics. Add real API kubelet-equivalent repeated POSTs against an existing Node, kubelet restart, concurrent creates and a delayed original create; unchanged existing nodes must retain one usable interlock and remain ordinarily drainable. Do not timeout-reclaim a possibly committing create.

findings.summary: All-Node coverage has no recovery branch for nodes that correctly have no metadata store.
findings.evidence: admission-contract.md:75-81 intentionally anchors every Node, not only storage members. :127-141 then requires a live metadata store and full relevant earned ISR to retire/release any reserved slot. design.md:86 explicitly requires nonstorage management nodes; ordinary nonstorage workers are also enrolled. A candidate with no relevant chunks can pass the eligibility reduction, but after its drain, cancellation, or required anchor refresh, it can never satisfy the unconditional live-store recovery predicate. One such reservation permanently occupies the global slot and blocks subsequent storage drains even after the node is healthy and uncordoned. If absence is instead classified as Unknown, its own ordinary drain cannot progress at all. No nonstorage path or corresponding fixture is defined.
findings.fix: Define exact classification and slot lifecycle for an enrolled Node with no metadata store/holdings, including later storage registration and conservative identity ambiguity. Permit safe ordinary nonstorage retirement/recovery without inventing store liveness, while preserving precommit all-Node coverage. Add nonstorage-node drain, uncordon/cancel, terminal/image refresh and later-storage-registration fixtures showing slot release and no coverage gap.

findings.summary: Old-Node retirement asks metadata to distinguish an old Kubernetes UID that its records do not carry.
findings.evidence: reader-contract.md:107-115 requires a unique metadata-node-to-Kubernetes-UID mapping, and admission-contract.md:143-148 releases a deleted/recreated Node only when no exact earned/current/move reference to the old node identity remains. The enrollment representation at admission-contract.md:37-39 stores name/NodeUID/current anchor but no metadata ID or observed store identity. Actual meta.proto:63-75 contains a node ID and labels without Kubernetes UID; current CSI node.go:20-21 equates that ID with the Kubernetes name. Reviewed #90 adds exact (node,device_uuid) refs and current store generation, but no Kubernetes UID. With old and new enrollments sharing a name, and a replacement store on the new UID retaining legitimate current refs under that metadata ID, the specified reader has no defined join or saved old-store predicate to evaluate the release condition. A node-name test holds forever on the new refs; simply binding to the new UID does not prove old refs absent.
findings.fix: Define the canonical metadata/Kubernetes identity join and persist the information actually needed for old-enrollment retirement, including how same-name new-UID and same/different returning stores are classified. Express the absence proof in fields actually supplied by metadata and retain conservative handling of unknown mappings. Add old/new same-name UIDs with old earned refs, successful replacement/move away from the old exact store, returning original store, restart and external-ID conflict fixtures; the legitimate replacement must have an explicit eventual release path.

findings.summary: The encoded receive caps do not enforce the promised decoded-memory bound before generated protobuf allocation.
findings.evidence: reader-contract.md:70-78 promises4096-node/64MiB encoded-plus-decoded bounds checked before allocation, but specifies only ordinary4MiB gRPC and512KiB page receive caps. Actual pinned grpc1.85.0 rpc_util.go:1051-1064 calls codec.Unmarshal after its encoded/decompressed size check; encoding/proto/proto.go:85-97 materializes the payload and calls proto.Unmarshal. Protobuf1.36.12 internal/impl/codec_field.go:568-588 creates/appends each repeated message while decoding, before the collector sees the response. A <=4MiB ListNodesResponse containing repeated empty nodes can instantiate roughly two million Node objects, far past4096 and64MiB before semantic rejection. Four in-flight decodes can multiply the excess. ListNodes still uses unbounded KV.List on the server (service.go:239-270); no predecode cardinality/allocation mechanism is defined for any response. Local dependency sources were read at the versions pinned in go.mod.
findings.fix: Specify a bounded production decoding/transport path that checks nested counts, lengths and an allocation charge before generated message construction and reserves transient decode memory within the process-wide budget. Cover all four permitted response types and full/paged nested messages, not just retained accumulator entries. Add real gRPC boundary/+1 malformed repeated-message and nested-message expansion fixtures asserting bounded allocations and no partial eligibility; retain existing receive limits.

findings.summary: The admission bounds leave pre-handler connections and slow request-body waits unspecified.
findings.evidence: design.md:69-74 bounds active HTTP handlers, body bytes and validator work, and security-contract.md:59-60 bounds decoded review depth. Neither defines accepted connection/TLS-handshake limits, header/idle/body read deadlines, maximum headers or HTTP/2 stream handling. A handler semaphore does not bound idle/pre-header sockets or concurrent TLS handshakes. A byte cap and request-context cancellation do not themselves impose a deadline on a peer that keeps a connection open while slowly sending its body. This exposes a new cluster-wide fail-closed listener to socket/worker exhaustion. Go1.27.4 net/http Server documents independent ReadHeaderTimeout, ReadTimeout, WriteTimeout and IdleTimeout with no timeout for zero values: https://pkg.go.dev/net/http#Server . Existing control/failover/kube.go is an outgoing client, not an inherited bounded HTTPS admission server.
findings.fix: Define bounded listener/handshake/connection and protocol settings plus finite header/body/write/idle deadlines that include decode and unwind work within the admission timeout. Keep rejection nonblocking and cancellation able to terminate actual reads, with bounded outstanding goroutines/buffers under HTTP/1 and any enabled HTTP/2. Add slow TLS/header/body, idle-connection and stream/concurrency boundary fixtures proving resource reclamation and recovery of legitimate API requests. Authentication remains separately required.

R1-C3/SEC91-R1-04 define the exact metadata-ID/name join, persisted immutable UID and saved exact-store evidence, returning-store/moved-away retirement, external collisions and conservative unknowns. These are concrete proposed fixes awaiting fresh incremental review; source63 remains dependent and no transferred finding is declared resolved merely by this text.
