findings.summary: The new predecode memory reservation still leaves gRPC HTTP/2 transport allocations outside its bound.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/91/reader-contract.md:109-117 reserves 2*receiveLimit+64KiB+1MiB per call and promises all four raw/decoded calls plus retained views remain in the same64MiB pool, but specifies neither client flow-control windows nor received header-list limits. In pinned grpc1.85.0, internal/transport/http2_client.go:405-411 enables BDP growth by default; bdp_estimator.go:27-30 permits16MiB windows; http2_client.go:1199-1217,1222-1301 grows each stream and queues incoming DATA before CodecV2 runs; transport.go:90-139 stores this in recvBuffer. A hostile metadata peer can send additional unary-response DATA while a valid first response is decoding, so the 4MiB/512KiB message cap does not cap queued transport bytes. Four warmed16MiB stream backlogs alone consume the entire pool before raw messages/retained views. Independently, defaults.go:47 permits16MiB received header lists before the codec, exceeding even a full-response reservation and far exceeding a page reservation. Structural Pass1 cannot prevent these prior allocations. Primary sources: [BDP limit](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/v1.85.0/internal/transport/bdp_estimator.go), [transport queue and flow control](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/v1.85.0/internal/transport/http2_client.go), [header defaults](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/v1.85.0/internal/transport/defaults.go).
findings.fix: Specify concrete client transport limits and account their maximum live memory in the existing pool: disable BDP with pinned grpc.WithStaticStreamWindowSize/WithStaticConnWindowSize (including the per-message adjustWindow allowance), set a small explicit grpc.WithMaxHeaderListSize, and bound/count live transports and frame/HPACK/queue scratch. Keep receive caps and fail before opening a call when reserved credit is unavailable. Add malicious real-HTTP2/gRPC fixtures that warm BDP, send extra unary-response DATA while decode is paused, and hit header/trailer-list boundary/+1; assert combined transport/decoded/retained high-water usage and reclamation, including512KiB pages and four calls. The [pinned public dial options](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/v1.85.0/dialoptions.go) supply the necessary controls; no dependency plan needs reopening.

rounds.resolution: SEC91-R2-01 is addressed by a concrete bounded guard gRPC transport: static stream/connection windows with BDP disabled, explicit header/buffer limits, four single-endpoint/single-call transport leases without overlapping replacement, bounded decrypted HTTP2 frame admission before gRPC parsing, pinned control-buffer throttling and receive compaction, and exact up-front lease/E(R)/decoded reservations in the existing64MiB pool. The draft includes per-message adjustWindow, tiny DATA/frame/queue/compaction/HPACK overhead and actual cleanup before credit reuse. Full-response concurrency is reduced rather than overcommitting. This proposed correction awaits fresh R3 source/contract review, especially actual pinned BufferPool minimum allocation and queue/compaction overhead for worst-case tiny frames; arithmetic alone is not a verified transport bound. No clear dependency or runtime source is changed. Historical approvals and source choice remain separate; revisions unapproved. No runtime/dependency/lab changes.

findings.summary: The transport reservation releases pooled response memory from its accounting while grpc still retains it, and its DATA-capacity proof also omits padding.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/91/reader-contract.md:167-184 defines 4*Q+256KiB from retained payload/object capacity and an exact invariant containing only live leases, calls and decoded candidates; :186-190 returns call/lease credit once codec buffers are free and ConnEnd arrives. None of the listed options replaces grpc's default buffer pool. Pinned grpc1.85.0 dialoptions.go:726 selects mem.DefaultBufferPool(); mem/buffer_pool.go:42-47 has 4KiB/16KiB tiers; internal/mem/buffer_pool.go:240-261 allocates tier capacity and Put stores it in sync.Pool. mem/buffers.go:155-180 shows Free returns the response backing slice to that pool, rather than releasing retained storage. ConnEnd in internal/transport/http2_client.go:1108-1112 neither purges nor accounts for it. A full response fragmented into approximately4093 1025-byte DATA frames fits the4096-frame ingress cap and can leave approximately16MiB of 4KiB-tier backing after the call unwinds. Subsequent16KiB-frame page calls use another tier, while the invariant admits retained D and new calls as though the old tier had disappeared; no GC/pool-drain condition or persistent cache reservation is specified. Separately, http_util.go:549-594 allocates from fh.Length before stripping padding: a length1025 padded frame with padSize255 retains769 bytes in4096 capacity. transport.go:155-162 evaluates Len, so these frames reset compaction instead of being coalesced. A source-flow arithmetic trace for a512KiB message plus permitted backlog retains752 such roots: backing plus root/handle, raw-fragment and queue-entry minima total3,159,520 bytes versus the stated raw+4Q+256KiB component3,145,728 bytes, before rounding/extra capacity. This disproves that component's claimed proof; it alone is not asserted to prove a whole64MiB overflow because other reserved slack can mask it.
findings.fix: Specify an explicit allocation policy for the pinned client, rather than assuming Free/ConnEnd removes pool retention. The existing exported experimental.WithBufferPool accepts a guard-local mem.BufferPool without a fork/internal import: use an exact-capacity noncaching policy or keep bounded cached capacities charged globally across calls and cleanup until actually dropped/reused. Re-derive DATA/fragment/backlog and compaction charges using actual allocated capacity including padding; update E(R)/concurrency only as needed. Add the future real-HTTP2 fixture for alternating1025-byte/16KiB frame tiers across completed calls, and padded1025-byte frames with255 padding, with charged cached/live capacity and subsequent credit reuse asserted. Preserve the existing receive caps and authority rules.

rounds.resolution: SEC91-R3-01 now specifies the actual exported experimental.WithBufferPool with a guard-local exact-capacity, noncaching allocation/Put policy and a lifetime ledger, with shared/default response-buffer caches excluded. Reader credits remain held for actual capacities, small-frame bypass references and call/transport cleanup; Free/ConnEnd is not treated as a garbage-collection or pool-purge signal. BoundedH2Conn rejects PADDED DATA before forwarding its frame header/allocation, an explicit direct pinned-peer profile whose stock writer uses unpadded DATA. The raw/queue/compaction/root/backlog proof is re-derived for that allocation policy and profile, retaining existing receive limits and64MiB budget. Alternating frame tiers across completed calls, padded-frame zero-allocation and later credit reuse are named fixtures. These proposed corrections await fresh R4 source/contract review; the earlier component defect is not exaggerated into an unproven whole-pool overflow. Historical approvals and source choice remain separate; revisions unapproved. No runtime/dependency/lab changes.

findings.summary: The new cache-free cleanup claim overlooks gRPC control-item pools that retain payloads and entire transport/stream reference chains after ConnEnd.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/91/reader-contract.md:139-141 says fixed cached bookkeeping is cleared and has no payload references; :207-224 charges scratch only to live leases and permits reuse after ConnEnd/call unwind/empty exactPool ledger. Pinned grpc1.85.0 internal/transport/controlbuf.go:42-87 instead returns itemNode to a process-global sync.Pool without clearing temp.it or temp.next. incomingSettingsHandler (:743-745) leaves incomingSettings.ss intact, so settings arrays from http2_client.go:1341-1365 remain reachable through cached nodes independently of exactPool. More substantially, a cached cleanupStream retains onWrite: http2_client.go:1005-1020 captures t and s, and cleanupStreamHandler (controlbuf.go:883-909) invokes but never clears it. Those closures can retain the old transport, stream, framer and receive-buffer references after ConnEnd. For <=1024 DATA, SliceBuffer.Free is a no-op (mem/buffers.go:306-317), so framer.dataFrame.data can still point to payload backing while the exact-pool ledger is empty. Replacing the response BufferPool and disabling shared transport buffers does not replace itemNodePool. This disproves the claimed cleared-bookkeeping/cleanup component; no whole64MiB overflow is asserted.
findings.fix: Account for pinned internal cached nodes and their full reference chains across completed call/lease-credit reuse, using a concrete process-wide persistent reservation/lifetime rule, or specify a concrete integration change that truly clears those references. Do not assume the exported response pool controls this separate cache or that ConnEnd purges it. Reconcile the retained capacity with D and the same64MiB invariant, and add a future stock-transport fixture covering cached incomingSettings/cleanupStream after success/error and <=1024 DATA, including a subsequent rotated call while prior cached references remain reachable. Preserve the no-internal-import/no-fork statement only for the mechanism actually specified.

findings.summary: Waiting for a Put-empty exactPool ledger permanently strands credits when stock gRPC abandons an unread response root.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/91/reader-contract.md:134-138 retires ledger entries only in Put, and :219-224 requires the ledger to be empty before releasing the call/lease; :373-381 expects error/cancel cleanup and later reuse. A permitted unpadded1025-byte DATA frame whose first5 bytes advertise a gRPC message length R+1 is a concrete counterexample. http_util.go:549-552 allocates it through exactPool.Get; transport.go:353-365 and mem/buffers.go:228-240 consume only the5-byte message header and retain the rest in recvBufferReader.last. rpc_util.go:783-797 then returns ResourceExhausted before reading the body. stream.go:1333-1347 closes the transport stream; http2_client.go:981-1036 merely queues the terminal error/cleanup and closes done, and :1039-1113 closes the connection and reports ConnEnd. None drains r.last or invokes its Free/Put, and there is no root finalizer in mem/buffers.go. Thus call unwind and transport cleanup can finish with an entry which will never receive Put; if the ownership ledger retains its handle, that ledger also keeps the backing alive. Four such completed failures can permanently consume all four leases even after a healthy metadata peer returns. This is a deterministic abandoned-root path, rather than an unknown or still-running cleanup.
findings.fix: Specify an implementable terminal per-call ownership-retirement/drain mechanism for roots abandoned by stock gRPC, with explicit quiescence conditions that exclude late reads/Get/Put and a safe late-Put policy; ordinary last-reference Put remains the normal path. Merely keeping credits forever or assuming every allocated root eventually calls Put does not satisfy the promised recovered normal call. Add the future real-HTTP2 R+1 length/1025-byte single-frame fixture, plus cancellation/codec rejection with queued or partially consumed DATA, and assert actual reclaim/reuse within the stated lifecycle while retaining credit for genuinely active references.

rounds.resolution: SEC91-R4-01/02 are addressed by the smaller explicit resource-lifecycle contract. Withdraw the unsupported whole-stock-gRPC64MiB live-credit proof and remove custom exact-pool/PADDED/frame-proof machinery whose only purpose was that proof. Use stock pinned gRPC with ordinary receive/header/concurrency/deadline controls and bounded typed application data;64MiB is application-controlled reader credit, not total private-library/runtime reachability. Actual containment is a verified cgroup-v2 memory.max≤256MiB/swap0 configuration with honest kernel reclaim/OOM semantics. Receive/transport/decode/cancel/resource failure enters Quiescing, refuses new admission, preserves uncertain durable writes/slots and exits75 for supervised replacement. Only process termination releases private stock caches/abandoned roots; no Put/ConnEnd/forced-Free or same-process cleanup claim remains. Healthy-call recovery is qualified across the observed old-process death and fresh startup. Proposed restart/backoff/held-maintenance costs are explicit and require human acceptance; S1/S4 and data authority are not narrowed. No maintained fork, new cleanup API or dependency source change is selected. These corrections await fresh R5 review of the final simplified contract. Historical approvals and source choice remain separate; revisions unapproved. No runtime/dependency/lab changes.

findings.evidence: Changed design.md:85 now specifies validator≤24s. Its normative admission-contract.md:150-153 still prescribes20s reader plus remaining≤8s of validator28s. security-contract.md:171-178 instead makes24s cover body/decode/validation/reply/unwind and stops actionable work by23s. An implementer following admission step3 can continue Kubernetes reads/CAS after the reply/cleanup deadline; the new design limit has not been propagated to its dependent procedure.
